P1 — at most one identifier of each type on a legal entity (a cross-field rule over the embedded list).
P2 — an LEI, where present, is unique across the whole register (a rule across rows, not within one).

The bean's standard screens — a searchable register of legal entities and the one-row edit form — are the whole surface. The register is reference data read constantly by other processes and edited rarely: a dense list, name and identifiers visible at a glance, search by name or identifier value. On the form, the identifier rows show type and value side by side so an LEI is readable without opening anything.

FCY standing rule R7 (from the company corpus) — every counterparty identified with an LEI; no free-text counterparty names. This register is where that LEI lives, but R7 binds at trade booking, not here: the register also holds FCY's own two booking entities, which face nobody and carry no LEI, so the bean deliberately leaves the identifier list optional. The later
/booking spec enforces R7 against this register.
FCY standing rule R8 (from the company corpus) — CDM enum values verbatim, never a house-specific string where a CDM enum exists.

Volume is the firm's counterparty population — roughly 40 active counterparties plus FCY's own two entities; no performance target beyond the platform's defaults. Considered, none apply: authorization (any signed-in user, the platform's default), availability, audit, privacy and retention, locale and time zones, cost.
A1 (verifies P1): WHEN a legal entity is saved carrying two identifiers of the same type, THEN the system SHALL reject the save.
A2 (verifies P2): WHEN a legal entity is saved carrying an LEI already held by another legal entity, THEN the system SHALL reject the save.
A3 (verifies P1, P2): WHEN a legal entity is saved with one identifier of each of two different types, THEN the system SHALL accept the save.
None — new bean, nothing to migrate. The register starts empty; FCY's own two entities and the ~40 counterparties are entered as ordinary rows when the feature lands.
entity — the firm's register of legal entities, searchable and editable — carrying an embedded
list. One edit form per bean, one listing for the register.
Implied by the bean blocks in the Data model and regenerated by the platform - do not edit this block; author above it what the catalog cannot derive.

LegalEntity - persistence.entity (persistence): The entity class with its builder, its descriptor + jsontype entry, its migration and table, and its tests; the descriptor is authored at spec time as the bean's entity-descriptor attachment (entity_descriptors/{qualified-descriptor-name}.json).
LegalEntity - observer.sheet (observer): The observer sheet: the entity's only remote surface, reads and writes.

LegalEntity - ui.defaultForm (ui): The default form of one row, rendered wherever the row is viewed or edited: its layout JS, authored at spec time as the spec's ui/{qualified-descriptor-name}.js attachment and shipped beside the entity class.

EntityIdentifier - embeddedBean (bean): A bean another bean embeds: its class with its builder, its descriptor + jsontype entry and its tests - a plain bean with NO persistence descriptor, so no migration, no table and no sheet; it lives inside the row of the bean that embeds it, and its descriptor is authored at spec time as its entity-descriptor attachment (entity_descriptors/{qualified-descriptor-name}.json).

EntityIdentifier - ui.defaultForm (ui): The default form of one row, rendered wherever the row is viewed or edited: its layout JS, authored at spec time as the spec's ui/{qualified-descriptor-name}.js attachment and shipped beside the entity class.
